name: CarpVM
listed_description: "interesting" VM in C. Let's see how this goes.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable and no speed claim at all. README (opened) is a pre-alpha register/stack VM description with an instruction table and says 'THIS PROJECT IS UNSTABLE AND DEPRECATED' (successor RabbitVM); it says recursion is untested. The repo tree (examples, extras, fuzz, src, tests, TODO.md, SYNTAX.md) has no benchmark directory; the repo page shows GPL-3.0, 984 stars, archived by the owner on 2021-01-19.

name: ChaiScript
listed_description: An easy to use embedded scripting language for C++. [BSD] [website](https://chaiscript.com/)
reason: Every number found shows ChaiScript slower than the recognizable baselines, and its maintainer says so. Scriptorium (r-lyeh-archived/scriptorium README and bench.csv, 2015, AMD A10 3.8 GHz, VS2013/2015, recursive fib): ChaiScript 175.038 s versus PUC Lua 1.341 s, Duktape 9.544 s, MicroPython 2.842 s; it is ahead only of 42tiny-js (227.170 s) and lil (555.976 s), which are not recognizable baselines. Gist totalgee/640805cb8995cf588152 (2015, Mac Pro Xeon E5 3.7 GHz, loop sum): ChaiScript 0.1898 to 0.4949 s versus Lua 5.3.0 0.0098 s, Python 2.7.6 0.0413 s, Node.js 0.0028 s. ChaiScript issue #189: ChaiScript 5.7.0 4.73 s versus Lua 5.1 0.36 s (sum), 31.01 s versus 0.35 s (primes), and the maintainer replies 'ChaiScript will never be as fast as Lua or JavaScript at math' and 'ChaiScript excels at calling C++ functions, not at math'. The README (opened, readme.md) and the performance_tests directory (profile scripts only, no comparison) make no speed claim against another engine; the only gain the maintainer cites is 'almost 100x faster than ChaiScript 1.0', a self comparison. Florian-Thake/BenchmarkScripts-TeaScript-VS-ChaiScript-VS-Jinx links results on blocked articles. BSD licence, 3.1k stars.
